content.content:
Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Then do what I put on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2\", \"title\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"name\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"revisionId\": \"1b0d9b5d65\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:00:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:41:00Z\", \"text\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\\nLeonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.\\n\\nWho to look at\\nEvery name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.\\n\\nGroups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)\\nGo by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.\\nNew investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.\\nIn talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.\\nAwaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.\\nKeep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.\\nEveryone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.\\nPassed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.\\n\\\"Us\\\" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.\\nAccelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.\\n\\nBuild access\\nFor firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.\\n\\nSheet\\nOne row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2", "title": "Q4 investor update - send list", "name": "Q4 investor update - send list", "revisionId": "1b0d9b5d65", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T18:00:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T18:41:00Z", "text": "Q4 investor update - send list
Leonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.

Who to look at
Every name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)
Go by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.
New investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.
In talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.
Awaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.
Keep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.
Everyone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.
Passed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.
"Us" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.
Accelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.

Build access
For firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.

Sheet
One row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Key Takeaways from the Pitch
• [PERSON_NAME_9160] was *most excited* about our *engine capabilities* rather than specific game titles.
• 
• Apple’s game categories:
• 
    ◦ *Cozy Games* → Targeting 7-25 y/o females (e.g., Animal Crossing players on Switch, Hello Kitty Arcade players).
    ◦ *Kid Games* → Under 7 years old, designed to keep kids engaged.
    ◦ *Classic Games* → Solitaire, Hearts, etc.
    ◦ *Match-3 Games* → Low adoption but good retention; Apple recognizes better F2P alternatives exist and won’t Push a match-3 subscription.
    ◦ *Puzzle Games* → Broad category with potential opportunities.
• *Where We Fit:*
• 
    ◦ We are positioned *between puzzle and classic games*.
    ◦ [PERSON_NAME_9160] is particularly interested in *Dominoes & Tri-Peak Solitaire*.
    ◦ *Solitaire is dominated by MobilityWare*, making it difficult to compete for Apple’s interest.
    ◦ However, a *custom-built Tri-Peak Solitaire or Dominoes game for Apple* would be a strong opportunity.
[PERSON_NAME_9160]’s Feedback on Our Games
• *Domino Delights*
•

Here’s how your idea could violate various ad network policies:
1. *Incentivized Ad engagement (Against AdMob & Most Networks)*
    ◦ Google AdMob *explicitly prohibits* rewarding users for watching ads unless it’s a rewarded ad format tied to in-app content (e.g., extra lives, virtual currency).
    ◦ Your model directly incentivizes users to watch ads for real-world payouts, which is *not allowed*.
2. *Artificial engagement / Invalid Traffic*
    ◦ Ad networks analyze user engagement, and if they detect that people are watching ads only for money (not genuine interest), they may classify the traffic as *invalid* and withhold earnings.

    ◦ If you’re paying users a portion of ad revenue, some networks may see this as *ad arbitrage*—where the intent is not genuine app usage but merely generating ad views.
    ◦ Networks like AdMob *ban ad revenue-sharing schemes* that exist solely to funnel money to users.
4. *Bot & Fraud Detection Risks*
    ◦ Many ad networks use sophisticated fraud detection systems. If a large percentage of users are just watching ads to earn money, it could trigger *fraud flags* and get your account banned.

TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.\\n\\nLeonard and team,\\n\\nThanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It\\u2019s obvious this isn\\u2019t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you\\u2019ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.\\n\\nAfter reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we\\u2019ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it\\u2019s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:\\n\\nThere\\u2019s a lot to like about what you\\u2019re building:\\n\\u2022 You\\u2019ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don\\u2019t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There\\u2019s a clear rhythm to how you\\u2019re executing.\\n\\u2022 We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Build a complete factual log of every investor-related email in Frederick Stone's mailbox (frederick.stone@harmonygames.co, use user_email "me"). The window is Sep 3, 2025 (when the HarmonyGames bridge / seed-extension SAFE round kicked off) through Sep 30, 2025 11:59pm Pacific (= Oct 1 06:59 UTC), plus anything after that up to Oct 1 07:00 UTC. Steps:
   - Fetch all 275 message ids from /tmp/ids0.json, /tmp/ids100.json and /tmp/ids200.json with mcp__hg__gmail_get_messages_batch.
     - First pass: format "metadata", to triage by subject/from/to.
     - Second pass: format "full" in batches of 10 or fewer for anything about investors, fundraising or partners.
     - Bodies are base64; decode them with python3 via Bash.
   - Run extra gmail searches to catch relevant mail outside that list, e.g. "bridge", "SAFE", "investment", "pitch", "intro", "Griffin", "speedrun", "TestFlight", "co-dev". This includes mail dated before Sep 3 or found in threads.
   - Report per firm or angel investor, chronologically, with exact dates and times.      - outreach, and who did it (Leonard, IH, Matthew, Griffin, advisors)
     - whether the contact was about the bridge/investment or about an RFP, partnership, co-dev, publishing or a service
     - calls or meetings held or scheduled

   - VCs and funds: London Venture Partners, Play Ventures, Transcend, Makers Fund, March Gaming, a16z / a16z speedrun, Hiro Capital, Grishin Robotics, Raine, General Catalyst, Lakestar, BBQ Capital, T-accelerate, Revo Capital, e2vc, Acterra, Core Finance, Turkish VCs (Gorkem Turk etc.)
   - Companies: NCsoft, Mattel, Sciplay, Superplay, Sony, Dentsu
   - Angels: Kevin Lin, Mike Fischer, Demetri Detsaridis, Anton Bernstein, Paul Heydon
   - Any other firm named in the messages
   Also identify, if possible, who the "Turkish VC" (Sep 29) was, and who the Sep 30 10:30am PDT VC meeting was with. The report must be exhaustive with precise quotes, and returned as the final text message with no files written.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Tools: mcp__hg__slack_* (slack_search_channels, slack_read_channel with oldest/latest/cursor/response_format, slack_read_thread, slack_search_public_and_private, slack_read_user_profile).

     - Aug 25, 2025 00:00 UTC = 1756080000
     - Sep 3, 2025 00:00 UTC = 1756857600
     - Oct 1, 2025 07:00 UTC = 1759302000
   - Pacific time in this period is PDT, which is UTC-7.

   No files are involved.
   - #bridge-pitch: id C096HFA5Z8W, private, 8 members, created by U04UP2L1RUY on 2025-07-20.

   - Read #executives (C07C2866011) with oldest=1756857600, latest=1759302000 and response_format concise, paging with the cursor, and read its threads.

   - Steps:
     - Fetch all 275 message ids from /tmp/ids0.json, /tmp/ids100.json and /tmp/ids200.json with mcp__hg__gmail_get_messages_batch.
       - First pass: format "metadata", to triage by subject/from/to.
       - Second pass: format "full" in batches of 10 or fewer for anything about investors, fundraising or partners.
       - Decode the base64 bodies with python3 via Bash.
     - Run extra gmail searches for mail outside that list: "bridge", "SAFE", "investment", "pitch", "intro", "Griffin", "speedrun", "TestFlight", "co-dev", firm names, Leonard, "Q4 update", DocuSign, commitment. This includes mail before Sep 3 and mail found in threads.
   - Report per firm or angel investor, chronologically, with exact dates and times.
     - Firms: London Venture Partners, Play Ventures, Transcend, Makers Fund, March Gaming, a16z speedrun, Hiro Capital, Grishin Robotics, Raine, General Catalyst, Lakestar, BBQ Capital, T-accelerate, NCsoft, Mattel, Sciplay, Superplay, Sony, Revo Capital, e2vc, Acterra, Dentsu, GFR Fund, Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem Capital, Gorkem Turk / Turkish VCs, Core Finance, Progression Fund, BITKRAFT, Galaxy, LEGO Ventures, 1Up, Initial Capital, plus ANY other firm that appears.

     - Who reached out to whom, including outreach on our behalf by IH, Matthew Collins, Griffin (banker/advisor) or advisors.

     - Meetings or calls proposed or held.

   - Also report the full text of any email from Leonard about the Q4 update send list, and any email that changes a commitment amount.

content.content: {"result":"{\"mimeType\": \"text/markdown\", \"text\": \"# Q4 investor update - send list\\nLeonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.\\n\\n## Who to look at\\nEvery name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.\\n\\n## Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)\\nGo by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.\\nNew investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.\\nIn talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.\\nAwaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.\\nKeep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.\\nEveryone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.\\nPassed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.\\n\\\"Us\\\" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.\\nAccelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.\\n\\n## Build access\\nFor firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.\\n\\n## Sheet\\nOne row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.\\n\", \"id\": \"f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2\", \"name\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\"}"}

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   This is a read-only task. The user's constraint, verbatim: "DO NOT post, react, draft or modify anything."
   HarmonyGames ran a bridge (seed extension SAFE) round that kicked off Sep 3, 2025. The work has four parts:
   - Read #bridge-pitch (C096HFA5Z8W) in full, including every thread reply. Window: Aug 25, 2025 to Oct 1, 2025 07:00 UTC.
   - Read #executives (C07C2866011), including threads, from Sep 3 to Oct 1, 2025 07:00 UTC, using concise format and paging with the cursor.
   - Run slack_search_public_and_private with after:2025-09-02 for each of these terms: bridge, SAFE, investor, pitch, speedrun, a16z, NCsoft, Mattel, Dentsu, Griffin, TestFlight, tester, "internal test", co-dev, term sheet, pass, VC.
   - Report per firm or angel investor, chronologically, with exact UTC and Pacific timestamps and exact quotes. For each, cover:
     - outreach, and who did it (Leonard, IH, Matthew, Griffin, advisors)
     - whether the contact was about the bridge or about an RFP, partnership, co-dev, publishing or a service
     - calls or meetings
     - any no/pass: the quote, and who it was given to
     - commitments and amounts
     - SAFE signing (note that DocuSign Completed is the criterion for a new investor)
     - TestFlight or Google Play internal test access: who was added, on which platform, and any removals
   Firms to watch:
   - VCs and funds: London Venture Partners, Play Ventures, Transcend, Makers Fund, March Gaming, a16z/speedrun, Hiro, Grishin, Raine, General Catalyst, Lakestar, BBQ Capital, T-accelerate, Revo Capital, e2vc, Acterra, Core Finance, Turkish VCs (Gorkem Turk)
   - Companies: NCsoft, Mattel, Sciplay, Superplay, Sony, Dentsu
   - Angels: Kevin Lin, Mike Fischer, Demetri Detsaridis, Anton Bernstein, Paul Heydon
   - Any other firm named
   Also identify the Turkish VC (Sep 29) and the Sep 30 10:30am PDT VC meeting. The final output is a text message only; no files are to be written.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Tools: mcp__hg__slack_read_channel (oldest/latest/cursor/response_format concise), slack_read_thread, slack_search_public_and_private.
   - Time bounds:
     - Aug 25 = 1756080000
     - Sep 3 = 1756857600
     - Oct 1 07:00 UTC = 1759302000
   - PDT = UTC-7.
   - IDs:
     - EMPLOYEE_0038 = Leonard (CEO)
     - EMPLOYEE_0016 = likely IH
     - EMPLOYEE_0025 = builds/testers
     - EMPLOYEE_0008 = Frederick Stone
   - Background agents:
     - aabefb346ae085dff (email sweep) FAILED from autocompact thrashing. Its output file is /tmp/claude-0/-app/85b4a1ff-eee4-4d4b-ad2c-16821d8e0ffa/tasks/aabefb346ae085dff.output and may contain partial results.
     - affb267f7c60d8b0d ("Find investor build access tracking") is still running. Do not duplicate it. Its output is at /tmp/claude-0/-app/85b4a1ff-eee4-4d4b-ad2c-16821d8e0ffa/tasks/affb267f7c60d8b0d.output.

3. Data gathered:

   #bridge-pitch, page 1 (from the earlier summary). Key points:
   - Sep 28 18:51 UTC: Leonard notes speedrun acceptances are being announced and expects "a rejection letter"; also mentions an NCsoft friend's LinkedIn.
   - Sep 26 22:50:00 UTC (15:50 PDT): Leonard: "told Mattel we're passing on the Barbie RFP. since the kickoff that's only been an RFP conversation, we haven't pitched them the bridge".
   - Sep 25 19:46 UTC: trying to schedule with TapNation (game acquisition).
   - Sep 25 16:20:00 UTC (09:20 PDT): Leonard: "correction on Play Ventures: the no I pasted here on the 15th was what they told Griffin, not us. that's why I said they never answered us. it's still their no for this round, the \"discussing\" Robert heard via Applovin doesn't change that".
   - Sep 25 14:39:25 UTC (07:39 PDT): rejection email from [PERSON_NAME_7818] ("Hey Leonard ... away last week in Istanbul ... we won't be joining this round ... later-stage financing ... concentrated on studios in Turkey"). Firm unknown, possibly Turkish.
   - Sep 25 02:33 UTC: "15% chance to raise funding".
   - Sep 25 00:30 UTC: [PERSON_NAME_8105] from AppLovin says the Play Ventures contact is aware; "discussing".
   - Sep 24 01:33–01:52 UTC (Sep 23 18:33–18:52 PDT), Google Play testers, likely for Dentsu: "offer them the google link"; EMPLOYEE_0025: "I have to add them by email for google play to work"; Leonard: "ok, I'll ask for their emails then" … "done".
   - Sep 24 00:06:35 UTC (Sep 23 17:06 PDT): "we are meeting with Dentsu in 25 mins". Debrief at 01:30:52 UTC: "impossible to read what they think".
   - Sep 23 23:50–00:00 UTC, Play Ventures:
     - "They didn't respond"; "they don't invest in mobile content"; "I emailed them back on Sept 3rd".
     - Leonard: "[USERNAME_32018], Matthew or [PERSON_NAME_6550] didn't ping them either"; "we really didn't get much help from our advisors".
     - IH asked [PERSON_NAME_8105] (AppLovin) to reach out: "he said OK!"

   #bridge-pitch, page 2 (read this segment; ts 1758662335 back to 1758130519):
   - Sep 23 21:05–21:18 UTC (ts 1758661132–1758662335; ~14:05–14:18 PDT), EMPLOYEE_0016 re [PERSON_NAME_8105] (AppLovin):
     - "Gonna send him our pitch deck, is that OK?"
     - Leonard posted a pitch blurb including "We're raising a $2.5M seed extension", "backed by a $3M seed led by GRIFFIN GAMING PARTNERS", "17-person".
     - 1758661728 (21:08:48 UTC / 14:08 PDT), Leonard: "[USERNAME_16962] said no", then "or didn't respond", "I need to check what happened".
     - Discussion of AppLovin's market cap; IH: "Oh, $3 mil to invest, not to buy us"; Leonard: "I don't know if he can invest without board's approval".
   - 1758563861 (Sep 22 17:57:41 UTC / 10:57 PDT), Leonard: "reached out to bitkraft"; "one of their partners connected with me over linkedin". At 1758564794: "[EMAIL_168353], you guys are CCed" and "we need to talk to more VCs :disappointed:".
   - 1758228086 (Sep 18 20:41 UTC), IH: Match Day has been trying to raise for 6 months; "Recent one is $4 @ 12"; "recapped". Leonard: "I think for us $10M-$12M is fair".
   - Sep 18 ~14:00–15:56 UTC (ts 1758203670–1758210951), Homa:
     - 1758210489 (Sep 18 15:48:09 UTC / 08:48 PDT), EMPLOYEE_0008: "I think we should focus Homa on the co-dev investment path."
     - "...cleanest easiest path for [PERSON_NAME_1114] to Push through"; "a confused mind says 'no'".
     - 1758210943, Leonard (thread parent, thread_ts 1758210943.211579): "path 1- co-dev / publishing  path 2- engine onboarding ?" This thread needs reading.
     - Earlier messages discuss the pitch claim "50 levels in 48 hours", so a Homa call apparently happened before Sep 18 14:00 UTC.
   - 1758162585 (Sep 18 02:29:45 UTC / Sep 17 19:29 PDT), Leonard: "[PERSON_NAME_4063] is joining the conversation tomorrow with a16z"; "he liked us a lot last time - let's see if we can keep it up this time to get up to $1M from them"; "...we'll pitch to a room full of investors in 3 months likely closing the round next quarter if we get into the speedrun".
   - 1758147530 (Sep 17 22:18:50 UTC / 15:18 PDT), Leonard (thread parent, thread_ts 1758147530.732569): "talked to Matthew - he says it's almost impossible to raise based on the content/metrics for Harmony Games - he is gonna look at the engine material and will think about creative solutions". This thread needs reading.
   - 1758143833 (Sep 17 21:17:13 UTC / 14:17 PDT), Leonard: "schedule another VC call for Sep 29th, this time with GFR fund", "you guys are CCed", "courtesy of [PERSON_NAME_0205]", "at least we made 2 first rounds with him, that's a positive".
     - This suggests the Sep 29 Turkish VC may be GFR Fund. Verify.
   - 1758143899: "tomorrow for the a16z convo, we gotta bring our A-game"; "it's 10 mins".

===== Fri, 26 Sep 2025 15:16:23 -0700 | leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> -> PERSON_2574_NAME <PERSON_2574_EMAIL> | CC PERSON_0558_NAME <PERSON_0558_EMAIL>, robert@harmonygames.co, arthur.blake@harmonygames.co, PERSON_3663_NAME <PERSON_3663_EMAIL>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co> | Re: re-intros: Are (LVP) <> Leonard & [PERSON_NAME_0054] ([SOURCE_ORG_0001])
Hi PERSON_2574_NAME,

Thank you for the thoughtful note and the kind words. We completely
understand your perspective, and the sentiment around content and market
risk in puzzle IP right now is fair. When we reach the right growth phase,
we plan to expand the studio footprint to Turkey to take advantage of the
deep talent pool and government subsidies we qualify for (since we have a
[NATIONALITY_0151] co-founder), but the timing isn’t There yet.

I’m not worried about scaling UA when the product has the metrics, but I
agree that in today’s environment, distribution challenges add risk. If our
trajectory meaningfully changes and we reduce those challenges, I’ll be
sure to keep you in the loop.

Still, we really value the conversation, your vote of confidence means a
lot, and we look forward to finding a way to work together in the future.

Best,
Leonard

On Thu, Sep 25, 2025 at 7:13 AM PERSON_2574_NAME <PERSON_2574_EMAIL> wrote:

> Hey Leonard,
>
> Really sorry for the delayed reply, we were away last week in Istanbul and
> it was tough to find time to sync internally. Thanks again for walking me
> through the updates with [SOURCE_ORG_0001], I really enjoyed the conversation! I
> managed to catch up with the rest of the investment team and unfortunately,
> we won’t be joining this round.
>
> That said, I want to say how much we respect what you’re building. The
> speed at which you’ve been able to stand up the [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine and move
> from Domino Delights to Zombie Match 3D is impressive, and it’s clear the
> team has the right mix of experience and execution chops. Ultimately,
> though, we don’t feel [SOURCE_ORG_0001] is the right fit for us at this stage. The
> content and market risk around scaling a new puzzle IP in the current
> environment feels higher than we’re comfortable with. In addition,
> later-stage financing for mobile teams right now seems largely concentrated
> on studios in Turkey, which makes it harder for teams outside that cluster
> to attract the follow-on capital required to scale UA.
>
> We get this stuff wrong all the time but wanted to be candid about where
> we fell short in case it is helpful for the others conversations that you
> are having. We are wishing you all the best and will be cheering you on
> from the sidelines!
>
> Best,
>

===== Wed, 17 Sep 2025 22:24:09 -0700 | leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> -> PERSON_1126_NAME <PERSON_1126_EMAIL> | CC frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co>, PERSON_0387_NAME <PERSON_0387_EMAIL>, PERSON_3760_NAME <PERSON_3760_EMAIL> | Re: Intro: Danny, Michael (SciPlay) <> Leonard ([SOURCE_ORG_0001])
Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],

Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.

In parallel, we are testing mode variations across a spectrum that might
lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:
1- from auto-play boosters that cover clutch zombie moments so you can look
at zombies to strategize
2- a charge-meter booster that temporarily converts match-3 to single-tap
match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
fire so players can tap without watching the board
3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).

We will run these iterations as quickly as we can and keep what works
for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated
on our end.

Best,
Leonard

Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],

Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.

In parallel, we are testing mode variations across a spectrum that might
lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:
1- from auto-play boosters that cover clutch zombie moments so you can look
at zombies to strategize
2- a charge-meter booster that temporarily converts match-3 to single-tap
match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
fire so players can tap without watching the board
3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).

We will run these iterations as quickly as we can and keep what works
for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated
on our end.

Best,
Leonard

matures.

Hi PERSON_0491_NAME,

Thank you again for the time the other day - we really enjoyed the
conversation. Your vision to build a billion-dollar casual mobile empire,
and the systems and tooling required to get There, maps perfectly to our
long-term vision. We are a lean, senior team, so we have to build both the
growth machine and the games with limited people and capital, but if we can
pursue that goal together at an accelerated pace, it could be a
massive win-win for NCSoft and [SOURCE_ORG_0001].

I believe it makes the most sense to keep making internal games at [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Games at the moment because dogfooding is essential to building great
systems. That said, we think having a pilot game where we onboard one of
your assets into the [SOURCE_ORG_0001] stack and operate it would immediately
accelerate our learnings. We have already started mapping the people,
roadmap, and tech decisions we would make for such a collaboration,
including a lightweight SDK and Unity plugin.

Early next week Blake and I will share a more concise view of what the
world looks like with resources over 6, 12, and 36 months. In the meantime,
Blake will walk you through the platform and answer technical questions,
and we are happy to propose a concrete pilot scope. Everyone on our side is
excited to explore how we can win together.

If it is helpful, you can grab a time here:
https://calendly.com/leonard.hayes/45mins .We are flexible and can move things
around to fit your schedule.

Best,
Leonard

We now port the stack into a new title in about 4 months at production quality, so a small team can learn faster and reuse success.\\n*Engine progression*\\n\\u2022 *Phase 1 (complete):* AI as assistant. Standardized live service infrastructure, level gen prototypes, physics-based 3D puzzle layer, boosters, leaderboards, quests, calendars, season pass. Automated level generation with constraints, difficulty scoring, authorable event tooling, experiment harness, and self-serve tools for designers. Use live player data and reinforcement learning to adapt difficulty, rewards, and pacing. Move service execution toward \\u201cautopilot\\u201d with embedded analytics optimizing events across titles with human guidance.\\n*Traction and revenue*\\n\\u2022 *Domino Delights (live in small markets):*\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Avg daily playtime: *~30 minutes*\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Avg DAU over last 6 months: *~600*\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 ARPDAU: *~$0.10*\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Earlier retention reads landed below our scale bar (D7 in mid-teens, ~35% of D1), which capped LTV against CPI. We are not scaling this title. Domino Delights validated the engine\\u2019s content pipeline, physics, boosters, event systems, storefront, and offer framework. The game is now being positioned with a publisher while we reuse the stack on a better core.\\n\\u2022 *Zombie Match 3D (alpha, UK iOS tests):*\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Early signals at minimal polish: *~34% D1*, *~23 min day-0 playtime*, *~$4.50 CPI* (small n)\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Live service integration ~60% complete, with remaining features on a short horizon\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Next 4\\u20136 weeks: expand to *500+ levels*, complete polish/VFX, and scale tests to *2\\u20133k* users for stable reads\\n\\u2022  \\u2022 Gates to proceed: *\\u226545% D1*, *\\u226545% D7/D1*, *\\u2264$3.50 CPI* in UK iOS. Leonard,

Done. The bridge send list is in my Q4 2025 investor update folder as "Q4 update - send list" (Google Sheet, shared with you): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1RaVZzDwjTFVPpaXnX4bxpxVcfEjt2ucJBi2H9XEgjww/edit

It's as of end of day Tue Sep 30 PT. Counts by group:
- New investor: 0 firms, 1 angel (Anton Bernstein, $40K. His DocuSign Completed notice came in Sep 26)
- In talks: 8 firms, 1 angel (a16z, NCsoft, SciPlay, HOMA, T-Accelerate, Dentsu, Brightwater Games Fund, GFR Fund; plus Paul Heydon at $50K, whose SAFE is still unsigned)
- Awaiting reply: 14 firms, 0 angels
- Keep warm: 2 firms, 0 angels (LVP, Hiro Capital)

Three things to know:
- Build access for the firms in talks: T-Accelerate, NCsoft, Dentsu and Brightwater are iOS only for now. Arthur found yesterday afternoon that the Play investor tester list was never attached to the internal track. The other four only have the public store links, so they're marked none.
- Play Ventures is off because their no went to Griffin and we never had a call. Mattel is off because it was RFP-only. a16z stays In talks because the speedrun decision isn't their bridge answer.
- Trello: the Existing Investor Update card now has New investor, In talks and Awaiting reply checklists. There was no Keep warm checklist on the card, so I added one too. Everyone In talks or Awaiting reply has an "F/up with ..." card in To Do. The exceptions are Dentsu (Oct 1 meeting) and Makers (Oct 8 meeting), and NCsoft, where I commented on the existing "F/up with Anel" card instead of adding a new one.

Happy to go through it Monday.

Fred

content.text:
The send list, the Trello updates and your reply to Leonard are all finished ahead of Monday's review.

**Send list:** I made a Google Sheet called "Q4 update - send list" (the name the README asks for). It's in your Q4 2025 investor update folder and shared with Leonard: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1RaVZzDwjTFVPpaXnX4bxpxVcfEjt2ucJBi2H9XEgjww/edit. There's one row per firm or angel getting the update, with group, amount, build access and a short note on why. It's as of end of day Tue Sep 30 Pacific.

| Group | Firms | Angels |
|---|---|---|
| New investor | 0 | 1: Anton Bernstein, $40K (DocuSign completed Sep 26) |
| In talks | 8: a16z, NCsoft, SciPlay, HOMA, T-Accelerate, Dentsu, Brightwater Games Fund, GFR Fund | 1: Paul Heydon, $50K (said yes, not signed yet) |
| Awaiting reply | 14: Makers, Raine, General Catalyst, BBQ, Superplay, Sony Mobile, Revo, e2vc, Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem, Initial Capital, BITKRAFT, Treo VC | 0 |
| Keep warm | 2: LVP, Hiro Capital | 0 |

**Build access:** T-Accelerate, NCsoft, Dentsu and Brightwater are **iOS only**. Arthur's Linear log says they were added on both platforms, but his Sep 30 Slack message says the Android tester list was never actually switched on. The other four firms in talks only have the public store links, so they're "none".

**Trello:** On the Existing Investor Update card I added New investor, In talks and Awaiting reply checklists. Leonard's note assumed a Keep warm checklist already existed, but it didn't, so I added that too. I created 20 "F/up with …" cards in To Do. Dentsu and Makers don't have one because they already have meetings booked on Oct 1 and Oct 8. NCsoft already had a To Do card ("F/up with Anel…"), so I commented on that instead.

**Email:** I replied on Leonard's thread with these counts and the link. It went to Leonard only; Robert and Arthur, who were cc'd on his email, weren't copied.

Four calls you may want to check with Leonard on Monday:
- **Treo VC** is in Awaiting reply because Leonard sent them the bridge deck on LinkedIn on Sep 4, after they contacted him first.
- **General Catalyst** is in Awaiting reply even though the investor list says Leonard's email bounced. Leonard posted in #bridge-pitch that IH also reached out to them on Sep 12.
- **Play Ventures** is off the list: their no went to Griffin rather than us, which Leonard's rules count as a no, and we never had a call with them. **Mattel** is off because it was only ever an RFP conversation.
- **a16z** stays In talks, because the speedrun rejection isn't an answer on the bridge.
